sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Brunswick County, NC?
sections.html:
The Brunswick County Tax Office appraises and assesses real and personal property, keeps ownership and tax records, and collects current and delinquent taxes. It is in the David R. Sandifer Administration Building, 30 Government Center Drive, Bolivia, NC 28422.

The general phone line is 910-253-2829. Questions about relief programs go to 910-253-2811, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Bills, property record cards, tax certifications, a tax foreclosure list and land records are all reached from the tax office page on the county website.

Collections staff will set up a payment plan if you cannot pay a bill in full, so call before a balance goes past due rather than after.

sections.h2: What does the Brunswick County housing market look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Brunswick County has grown quickly, and its housing numbers sit well above those of the state's rural counties. Census QuickFacts estimates 174,702 residents in July 2025, up 27.8% from the April 2020 base of 136,695, on 850.08 square miles of land.

The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $349,800, with 84.6% of homes owner-occupied and a median gross rent of $1,351. About 36.6% of residents are 65 or older. The Census counted 4,457 building permits in 2025 and 116,023 housing units. New construction is one of the few things that changes a value between reappraisals.

The county's rate schedule lists 19 towns and villages, from Bolivia and Northwest to Holden Beach, Oak Island, Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, Caswell Beach, Bald Head Island, Leland, Navassa, Shallotte and Southport. Where a parcel sits decides which town rate is added to the county rate.

sections.h2: What is the Brunswick County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county rate is 0.3420, or 34.20 cents per $100 of value, and the county's schedule shows that same figure for 2024, 2025 and 2026. It fell from 0.485 in 2022 to 0.342 in 2023, the year of the last countywide revaluation.

The Department of Revenue's August 2024 schedule agrees with the county figure of .3420 and lists 2023 and 2027 as the last and next reappraisal years.

sections.h2: When is the Brunswick County revaluation, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
The next revaluation is effective January 1, 2027, and every parcel will be valued at its market value and condition on that date. A building still under construction on January 1 is appraised by its percentage of completion.

Notices showing the new assessed value are scheduled to go out between February and March 2027. Read the notice and compare it with the property record card to confirm the property information is correct. The review process has two steps:

  • Informal review: from January until the board of equalization and review convenes, the tax assessor can make lawful changes when the data warrants it.
  • Formal appeal: once the board convenes it controls changes, and the owner or a representative normally appears to present the case.

Appeals that arrive after the board convenes become formal automatically. Appeals that arrive after it adjourns are untimely and generally wait until the next year. A value change applies to the year the appeal is heard and forward, and it is not retroactive. Under G.S. 105-322, the board's first meeting falls between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, and a reappraisal-year board must finish by December 1. A taxpayer then has 30 days after the board mails its decision to take an appeal to the Property Tax Commission.

sections.h2: When are Brunswick County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1 and can be paid without interest through January 5, or the next business day if January 5 falls on a weekend. The 2026 bills were mailed in mid-August and can be paid without interest through January 5, 2027.

After that, interest starts under the state statute: 2% from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent a month from February 1 until paid. A mailed payment counts as paid on its postmark date. Some taxing units adopt prepayment discounts by May 1 resolution, so ask the tax office whether one applies.

The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, and unpaid real estate taxes can be enforced by a foreclosure action filed in the county.

sections.h2: Which property tax relief programs apply in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
Four programs are listed on the county's relief page. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, within the income limit. NCDOR lists $38,800 as the 2026 limit.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test, and an unmarried surviving spouse can also qualify.
  • Homestead circuit breaker: taxes limited to 4% of income, or 5% when income is above the limit but within 150% of it. The extra tax is deferred and remains a lien.
  • Present-use value: qualifying agricultural, horticultural or forestland is assessed at use value instead of market value.

Brunswick's county page states that the three most recent years of deferred circuit breaker taxes become due, with interest, on a disqualifying event: death, transfer of the property, or the owner leaving the home as a permanent residence. That means a sale triggers the bill. Applications are filed with the county tax office on the state form, within the January listing period, though the county must accept them through June 1.

sections.h2: What happens to Brunswick County taxes when you sell a house?
sections.html:
Brunswick County has a local rule: by resolution, a deed must be stamped by the tax office before it can be recorded at the Register of Deeds. The stamp confirms that taxes, fees and assessments are settled.

A Tax Certification, requested under G.S. 105-361 by an owner, attorney or other interested person, shows local tax liens, deferred taxes where they apply, fire fees and assessments the office must collect. Order it early, because deferred circuit breaker or present-use taxes show up there.

The state excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 of the consideration, paid by the seller to the Register of Deeds before recording.

If taxes go unpaid, the county sells the parcel at auction on the steps of the courthouse in Bolivia, rain or shine. Bidders pay a 5% deposit immediately by cash, certified check, cashier's check or money order, and the county does not offer financing. A 10-day upset bid period follows, and an upset bid must beat the last bid by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The winning bidder has one week after notice to pay in full and receives a commissioner's deed. An owner can still sell the house and pay the taxes at closing before that process finishes.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Brunswick County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Call 910-253-2829, or visit the office at 30 Government Center Drive in Bolivia. For tax relief questions, call 910-253-2811 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the Brunswick County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.3420 per $100 of value for 2024, 2025 and 2026, and town or district rates are added where they apply. Rates are normally adopted in late spring or early summer.

faqs.q: When is the next Brunswick County revaluation?
faqs.a: The next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, with value notices scheduled between February and March 2027. The last one was effective January 1, 2023.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Brunswick County property taxes late without penalty?
faqs.a: No. Taxes due September 1 are interest-free only through January 5, and interest starts the day after. Contact the collections division about a payment plan before the deadline.

faqs.q: Does Brunswick County require tax clearance to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. By county resolution, deeds must be stamped by the tax office before the Register of Deeds records them. The stamp confirms taxes, fees and assessments are taken care of.
